title: Explicit orchestrator-location signal (TICKS_ORCHESTRATOR), not inference
description:
Operator observation (2026-08-20), prompted by the first completed cloud run aborting on the repo-pinned herdr substrate.

Today nothing tells an orchestrator WHERE it is running. The skill detects the HARNESS by capability probes (Agent tools, rlm in globals, /ticks-run registered) and resolves the SUBSTRATE by probing for a herdr socket. Neither answers "am I a laptop or a container", so a cloud orchestrator reads a repo config written for a laptop and does the wrong thing — exactly what eb5 is fixing case-by-case.

Add an explicit signal the entrypoint sets and both tk and the skill honour: TICKS_ORCHESTRATOR=cloud (values: local | cloud). It generalises beyond substrate:
- substrate resolution: cloud implies harness in Phase 1, without probing for a socket that cannot exist.
- max_parallel and other [orchestration] keys tuned for a laptop should not silently govern a container.
- TK_ACTOR already carries cloud:orchestrator for PROVENANCE; this is the same fact available for ROUTING, so the two must agree rather than being derived separately.

Design constraints: absence means local, so nothing changes for existing users; the value is set by the sandbox entrypoint, never inferred from the environment; and a cloud orchestrator must still ANNOUNCE what it resolved and why, since the protocol requires explicit degradation to be stated rather than silent. Document it in the skill (agent-runner.md substrate section) alongside the existing probes, and note it in runners-config.md.

Coordinate with eb5, which is fixing the substrate case right now — this tick is the general mechanism, and eb5 should use it rather than a one-off.
